tier_reason: Upgraded from C to A on stronger evidence. The CI 'Library Comparison' comment on PR #5 (2026-08-25) runs the public bench/comparison_test.go through .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml: actions/setup-go go-version '1.25', `go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=3 -benchtime=100ms -run=^$` in bench/. Its raw output prints cpu: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor (linux/amd64), so code, compiler, flags and CPU model are all public, and the raw lines match the table. The bench/README Windows i7-1255U table alone would be C, since it states no Go version.

corrections.baseline: mattn/go-runewidth v0.0.19 (the de facto Go terminal display-width library) and rivo/uniseg v0.4.7 StringWidth, both pinned in bench/go.mod; HarfBuzz, FreeType and ICU are not involved
corrections.claimed_speedup: CI three-way comparison on PR #5 (AMD EPYC 7763, linux/amd64, Go 1.25, median of 3 runs), uniwidth vs go-runewidth vs uniseg: StringWidth ASCII short 6.06 vs 73.18 vs 112.2 ns (12.0x / 18.5x); ASCII medium 16.85 vs 625.1 vs 958.1 ns (37.0x / 56.8x); ASCII long 64.08 vs 3,327 vs 5,129 ns (51.9x / 80.0x); CJK short 69.40 vs 156.6 vs 204.7 ns (2.2x / 2.9x); CJK medium 711.2 vs 1,539 vs 1,987 ns (2.1x / 2.7x); mixed short 146.6 vs 255.8 vs 363.9 ns (1.7x / 2.4x); emoji short 151.3 vs 266.6 vs 392.7 ns (1.7x / 2.5x); flags 111.6 vs 232.0 vs 311.5 ns (2.0x / 2.7x); ZWJ 185.1 vs 217.5 vs 486.9 ns (1.1x / 2.6x); TUI table header 548.7 vs 686.0 vs 939.1 ns (1.2x / 1.7x). RuneWidth vs go-runewidth: CJK 2.50 vs 21.97 ns (8.7x), emoji 2.81 vs 13.26 ns (4.7x), ASCII 2.39 vs 2.81 ns (1.1x). The bench/README table (Intel Core i7-1255U, Windows) reports ASCII short 9 vs 107 vs 165 ns, ASCII long 340 vs 5,380 vs 8,058 ns, CJK short 96 vs 347 vs 379 ns, mixed short 173 vs 469 vs 632 ns, emoji short 158 vs 380 vs 534 ns, and ZWJ 323 vs 326 vs 691 ns. The top-level README headline is '3-46x faster than go-runewidth'.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Go 1.25 gc toolchain (actions/setup-go go-version '1.25'; the patch release is not printed); go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=3 -benchtime=100ms -run=^$ in bench/ (Library Comparison job in .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml). The bench/README Windows run used go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -run=^$ and states no toolchain version (bench/go.mod: go 1.25.1).
corrections.hardware: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, linux/amd64, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner, 4 procs (CI on PR #5); bench/README run: Intel Core i7-1255U, Windows, amd64
corrections.workload: RuneWidth on an ASCII, a CJK and an emoji rune, plus StringWidth on ASCII (5/43/228 chars), CJK, mixed, emoji, TUI (prompt, box-drawing table header, emoji status line), flag, ZWJ and combined strings, all in the separate bench/ module (bench/comparison_test.go). Results are discarded with `_ =`, and the widths are not cross-checked between libraries.
corrections.caveats: The numbers are first-party. The CI comparison runs on a shared GitHub Actions runner with -count=3 and -benchtime=100ms, and the workflow itself calls these results directional with 10-20% variance, which matters for the 1.1-1.4x rows (ZWJ, table header, combined). The work is not identical. go-runewidth v0.0.19 StringWidth runs full UAX #29 grapheme segmentation (clipperhouse/uax29/v2) on every string, ASCII included. uniwidth instead takes a SWAR ASCII path and a lightweight ZWJ/VS16/flag/skin-tone state machine without full segmentation. The Unicode tables differ too: 16.0 in uniwidth, 15.1.0 in go-runewidth (script/generate.go). Both treat East Asian Ambiguous as narrow by default outside CJK locales; go-runewidth picks the setting from RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN or the locale or console. The bench never checks that the libraries agree, and their outputs can differ on VS16 sequences (uniwidth forces any character followed by U+FE0F to width 2) and on clusters that only UAX #29 merges. go-runewidth's optional CreateLUT() lookup table is not enabled. The bench/README Windows table looks stale against the current code: it gives uniwidth ASCII long as 340 ns, against 64 ns in CI and ~50 ns in the CHANGELOG. The README headline '3-46x' overstates the low end, since non-ASCII StringWidth gains are 1.1-2.2x in CI. Display width is a text-layout primitive, not shaping. The baselines are Go libraries, not HarfBuzz, FreeType or ICU.

notes: Language Go, pure Go with zero dependencies (no assembly). go-runewidth is a recognisable incumbent for terminal width in Go, and uniseg is the Go UAX #29 reference. baseline_in_list stays false. The entry belongs in font-shaping-text-layout as a text-layout primitive (terminal cell width), not shaping. Metadata checked: MIT, 8 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-08-25.

tier_reason: The README section 'Performance: 40x faster than wcwidth' shows one IPython %%timeit session on one string: wcwidth 1.73 us, cwcwidth 211 ns, uwcwidth 41 ns. It names no CPU and no Python, wcwidth or cwcwidth versions, and the repo holds no benchmark script (only tests/test_uwcwidth.py). These are first-party numbers without methodology, which is C.

corrections.baseline: jquast/wcwidth, the standard Python terminal-width package, which was pure Python when measured (most likely 0.2.13, the only wcwidth release between January 2024 and September 2025 per PyPI); cwcwidth, a Cython binding to the C library's wcwidth/wcswidth, was also measured; neither version is stated
corrections.claimed_speedup: README IPython %%timeit of wcswidth('コンニチハ, セカイ!') gives wcwidth 1.73 us ± 7.93 ns, cwcwidth 211 ns ± 3.63 ns and uwcwidth 41 ns ± 0.0363 ns per loop. That is about 42x vs wcwidth and 5.1x vs cwcwidth (derived from page data). The README heading says 'Performance: 40x faster than wcwidth'.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the timing. The package is a Cython extension built with -O3 on non-MSVC compilers and with no extra flags under MSVC (setup.py). Python, wcwidth and cwcwidth versions are not stated.
corrections.workload: wcswidth of the 11-codepoint string 'コンニチハ, セカイ!' (full-width katakana plus ASCII) in IPython %%timeit, 7 runs of 10^6 or 10^7 loops; that one string is the whole benchmark.
corrections.caveats: The 40x comes from one short string with no CPU, OS or Python version, and the numbers are first-party. Most of the 40x is the gap between a compiled Cython extension (uwcwidth.pyx, -O3) and the pure-Python wcwidth of 2024. The like-for-like compiled comparison is cwcwidth, which uwcwidth beats by about 5x. cwcwidth's widths come from the platform libc, so its Unicode coverage varies by system. The baseline has since moved: wcwidth is at 0.9.1 (2026), describes itself as a Python and C11 library and ships platform abi3 wheels, and that version was not measured, so the 40x should be treated as stale. Semantics differ slightly. uwcwidth uses Unicode 16.0 (draft) tables derived from musl's wcwidth, skips the codepoint after a ZWJ unconditionally and forces width 2 on VS16. It returns -1 for control characters, as wcwidth does. The tests do not compare outputs against wcwidth. Terminal cell width is a text-layout primitive rather than shaping, and the baseline is a Python package, not HarfBuzz, FreeType or ICU.

notes: Language: Cython compiled to a CPython C extension, used from Python; the orchestrator may want language 'Cython' rather than 'Python'. wcwidth (jquast) is the recognisable incumbent for terminal width in Python. baseline_in_list stays false, and the entry belongs in font-shaping-text-layout as a text-layout primitive, not shaping. Metadata checked: MIT (portions from musl, also MIT), 4 stars, not a fork, last commit 2024-10-28, so stale is correct.
